overview: Single-centre diagnostic accuracy study validating pre-specified cut-offs of two bedside tests against the exercise-test anaerobic threshold in consecutive adults booked for major abdominal surgery.
population: Consecutive adults booked for colorectal, upper gastrointestinal, liver or pancreatic resection who attend pre-assessment at least three weeks before surgery; excluded are patients for whom exercise testing is contraindicated.
exposure: Index tests at pre-assessment by a physiotherapist: 30-second sit-to-stand (cut-off 10 or fewer) and four-metre gait speed (cut-off below 1.0 m/s), both pre-specified.
procedures: Exercise testing within two weeks by an exercise physiologist blind to the bedside results; the physiotherapist is blind to exercise results because testing follows. Anaerobic threshold is read by two physiologists independently, with a third for disagreement. Patients who start but cannot complete exercise testing are classified as reference positive (low functional capacity) in the primary analysis. Prehabilitation allocation continues by current practice during the study.

outcomes.name: Sensitivity of sit-to-stand 10 or fewer
outcomes.measure: Proportion of reference-positive patients with a count of 10 or fewer
outcomes.why: Triage must not miss unfit patients.

outcomes.name: Specificity of sit-to-stand 10 or fewer
outcomes.measure: Proportion of reference-negative patients with a count above 10

outcomes.name: Accuracy of gait speed and the combination
outcomes.measure: Sensitivity and specificity of gait speed below 1.0 m/s and of either test positive
outcomes.why: Candidate alternatives; exploratory for the combination.

outcomes.name: Unable to complete a test
outcomes.measure: Proportion unable to complete each index test and the reference test
outcomes.why: The untestable patients are the main source of bias.

feasibility: About 180 patients over nine months using 5 of the 12 weekly exercise test slots; bedside tests take under ten minutes.
biasMitigation: Pre-specified rule for incomplete reference tests

biasFlags.label: Spectrum bias
biasFlags.note: Patients seen late for pre-assessment are missed.

biasFlags.label: Incorporation of untestable patients
biasFlags.note: Classification rule tested in a sensitivity analysis.

parsimony.simplestPath: One index test, one cut-off, one reference standard.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond the accuracy study design.
summary: Consecutive-patient validation of two pre-specified bedside cut-offs against exercise testing.
